evidence.title: Anthropic reports access or attempted access beyond weakened inner sandboxes in524/1753 scenarios (30%); use of outside credentials/files in4%; nine secret-access cases, no host takeover.
evidence.observation: Anthropic reports access or attempted access beyond weakened inner sandboxes in524/1753 scenarios (30%); use of outside credentials/files in4%; nine secret-access cases, no host takeover. Most tasks needed unavailable internal inputs. A sandbox-description prompt reduced reaching attempts to1.8%.
evidence.limitations: One run per scenario, deliberately weakened inner boundary; internet-disabled Firecracker outer VM. Some routes were not recorded. Attempt/access, actual use and host takeover are distinct. Prompt clarification sharply reduced attempts; author says ambiguous boundaries sometimes explain reaching. Not production prevalence or evidence of escaping the outer containment.

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.
